blanks.sentence: Weather is experienced day by day, while climate describes _____ conditions.
Tropical storms are large systems with _____ movement.
In the Indian Ocean, these storms are called _____.
Scientists think storms may become _____ as they move across an area.
Rain over one area may last longer, increasing _____.
Compared with landslides, mudslides tend to be faster and _____.
After heavy rain, either kind of slide can damage _____.
Sea levels are getting _____; this may make surges more dangerous.
A surge may reach a height of _____.

multipleChoice.question: How does the opening distinction compare weather with climate?
options: Weather concerns longer periods than climate does.
Weather and climate describe the same time span.
Weather is experienced daily; climate spans longer periods.
Climate is observed only during tropical storms.

multipleChoice.question: Why do hurricanes, cyclones and typhoons have different names?
options: They develop in different parts of the world.
They rotate at different rates over water.
They reach different levels of destruction.
They form at different stages of warming.

multipleChoice.question: What change do climate scientists anticipate as the world warms?
options: Tropical storms will become easier to predict.
Tropical storms will become more destructive.
Tropical storms will form only in warmer seas.
Tropical storms will stop changing their names.

multipleChoice.question: How may slower movement make a storm more damaging in one area?
options: It reduces the wind but delays the rain.
It creates more storms over the same sea.
It keeps wind and rain over the area longer.
It moves floods away from populated areas.

multipleChoice.question: What limitation would a building-only assessment of landslides and mudslides have?
options: It would misidentify the place where a slide began.
It would overstate the damage suffered by buildings.
It would treat landslides as faster than mudslides.
It would overlook possible deaths and injuries.

multipleChoice.question: Why is a storm surge singled out as a major danger within a storm?
options: It is the only part of a storm that can move inland.
It can cause more casualties than any other element.
It prevents the storm's winds from becoming stronger.
It makes all other forms of flooding impossible.

multipleChoice.question: What drives the rapid rise of seawater during a storm surge?
options: Strong storm winds push the sea towards land.
Heavy rainfall pulls seawater into the clouds.
Moving rocks force seawater over the shore.
A falling sea level exposes the ocean floor.

multipleChoice.question: What follows from the two kinds of harm described when a surge reaches land?
options: Damage to buildings is the only harm to consider.
Protecting buildings would also protect every person.
People face danger only at the maximum surge height.
Protecting buildings alone may leave people at risk.
